title: Explicit Hamiltonian ball packings in every dimension
description:
Version 1.0.1, 29 October 2026. Manuscript, complete supplementary proofs, and Lean 4 formalisation by Liang Song.

For every integer k ≥ 10 and ε ∈ (0,1), one construction defines an explicit smooth compactly supported Hamiltonian whose time-one map packs the k closed unit balls in the four-ball of radius (k/(1-ε/4))1/4, with density 1-ε/4 and an explicit stability margin. The same construction realises every packing allowed by the volume and two-ball inequalities in dimensions 2n ≥ 6, and the range Σci2 < C2 and 3ci < C in dimension four. A uniform terminating oracle algorithm outputs a rational polynomial times a fixed cutoff; no practical runtime bound or executable competition submission is claimed.

The main packing, stability, and algorithm theorems are verified in Lean 4 with the pinned Mathlib dependency. Auxiliary paper labels distinguish full-statement verification from verification of the consequences used by the construction. The precise paper-to-Lean correspondence and remaining differences of form are documented in the manuscript formal-verification section and supplement Appendix A.5.

The archive provides the paper and supplement, source code, reviewer guide, reproducible verification scripts and CI configuration. External publication records, content hashes and timestamp evidence identify the frozen version; they document existence of the deposited content, rather than independently establishing mathematical novelty or authorship.

Source and verification guide: https://github.com/s-JoL/Symplectic-Ball-Packing. License: Apache-2.0; vendored components retain their original copyright and provenance notices.

Revision from 1.0.0. Corrects the relative Moser support bound to ||X||2 ≤ 6 and the rational-parameter existence argument using a nonempty real open set; updates the precise-support correspondence, CI replay documentation and scalar-mollifier comment. Lean definitions, theorem statements and proofs are unchanged. Verification receipts and the optional proof cache are regenerated for this version. The fixed GitHub release, source tree and reviewer guide correspond to this DOI. The original 1.0.0 archive remains available.
